#62640. How Do You Land on a Moon With Almost No Gravity?

📅 06 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 15m • 📚 Deep Dive (2949 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ieee ↗ Open Full Page

How Do You Land on a Moon With Almost No Gravity?

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 15 min read (2949 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ieee

⏱️ ~15 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Japan’s MMX mission aims to sample the Martian moon Phobos.
  • Japan's MMX spacecraft will fire its engines to slow down and enter orbit around Mars.
  • Recent findings suggest that last August, looking up from the edge of an ancient river delta on Mars, the Perseverance rover’s electronic eye spied an oblong shadow crossing the distant, glowing Sun.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Japan’s MMX mission aims to sample the Martian moon Phobos.

Japan's MMX spacecraft will fire its engines to slow down and enter orbit around Mars.

Recent findings suggest that last August, looking up from the edge of an ancient river delta on Mars, the Perseverance rover’s electronic eye spied an oblong shadow crossing the distant, glowing Sun. Phobos, the Martian moon named for the Greek god of fear and panic, was transiting the solar disk. Too small to darken the pale, dust-tinged sky, but orbiting close enough to eclipse a significant fraction of the Sun, Phobos passed in less than a minute.

NASA’s Perseverance rover captured Phobos passing in front of the Sun from the surface of Mars.ASU/MSSS/SSI/JPL-Caltech/NASA.

The tiny moon, with its murky origins, is an enigma, and one whose makeup and history could tell us much about Mars and the wider solar system. And now the international Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission, which successfully launched on 20 October, seeks to explore that mystery with an unprecedented series of landings on the unknown surface of Phobos.

Industry observers note that this mission brings unusual challenges—for example, designing an orbit to study a microgravity moon orbiting a much larger planet. Engineers also had to figure out how to assess and land on this low-gravity pile of loosely assembled dirt and rock, how a rover might rove across it, and how the spacecraft might take samples and return them to Earth.

“I often say that landing on Phobos is like trying to land a balloon,” indicates Yasuhiro Kawakatsu, project manager of MMX at the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA). “It’s very difficult to drop a balloon to the ground and prevent it from tilting or bouncing.”.

Sources indicate that phobos is one of two small Martian moons; the other is Deimos, named after the Greek god of dread and terror. Their cosmic origins are unknown, though there are two prevailing theories. One holds that the moons were once asteroids from the belt between Mars and Jupiter, captured by the smaller planet’s gravity. In the other theory, Phobos and Deimos formed when a large celestial body slammed into Mars, sending debris into orbit. Some models suggest the pair are the last survivors from a cluster of satellites.

The enormous Stickney crater, roughly 9 kilometers across, dominates this view of Phobos taken by NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter.University of Arizona/JPL-Caltech/NASA.

Scientifically speaking, Phobos is considered a rubble pile, a loosely consolidated aggregate of rock and dust. Far too small to become spherical under its own mass, it’s shaped like a lumpy potato, roughly 27 kilometers in length, with only 1/1,800th of Earth’s gravity. On Phobos, a typical adult would weigh about as much as a tennis ball does on Earth.

More than 10 years in the making, MMX debuted on Japan’s flagship H3 rocket from Tanegashima spaceport on 20 October local time. It will arrive at Mars in 2027 carrying scientific payloads from several space agencies, including NASA, and a upcoming rover called Idefix developed by the French and German space agencies (CNES and DLR) in collaboration with JAXA.

Engineers assembled MMX’s modules at Japan’s Tanegashima Space Center before the spacecraft’s October 2026 launch.JAXA.

Recent findings suggest that MMX consists of three modules: a propulsion module to power its journey to Mars and apply the brakes to enter orbit around the red planet; an exploration module carrying the rover, sampling gear, and other scientific instruments; and a return module, attached to the exploration module, that harbors the capsule destined for a high-speed reentry into Earth’s atmosphere. After collecting samples on Phobos, the exploration and return modules will lift off together. The exploration module will then be jettisoned while the return module sets a course back home.

If all goes according to plan, MMX will deliver a 10-gram sample to Earth in the second half of 2031. But the mission will face a series of daunting challenges to reach that end point, including navigating complex orbits around Phobos and landing on its surface while Mars periodically blocks communications with Earth.

The MMX’s modular design includes the propulsion module [left] and the exploration and return modules [right].Kyodo News/Getty Images.

“It’s the most complex mission I have ever seen,” says Patrick Michel, director of research at CNRS (the French National Center for Scientific Research) and co-principal investigator on Idefix.

An H3 rocket carried MMX into space on 20 October 2026, beginning the mission’s five-year journey to Phobos and back.The Asahi Shimbun/Getty Images.

Once MMX reached low Earth orbit, its propulsion module’s engine fired, kicking off a nearly year-long deep-space cruise to Mars. On arrival, the spacecraft will need to fire its engines in an extended, carefully timed burn to slow down enough to be captured by Mars gravity. The propulsion module will then be jettisoned, leaving the exploration and return modules to orbit Mars.

“If something doesn’t go according to strategy, MMX will fly by Mars and get catapulted into the solar system,” says Nicola Baresi, an astrodynamicist who coauthored a paper on specially designed orbits for MMX.

It has been revealed that from that initial orbit, MMX will transition into a specially designed quasi-satellite orbit that allows it to keep pace with the small moon but also move around it. Since Phobos is too small to orbit in the conventional sense, the spacecraft will orbit Mars alongside the moon, following a clever egg-shaped path that slings MMX alternately ahead of and behind the moon. “When you’re closer to Mars, you’re accelerating with respect to Phobos, and when you’re farther from Mars, you’re decelerating. So you essentially go back and forth,” explains Baresi.

Martian Maneuvers To reach Phobos, MMX will execute three major maneuvers: MOI-1 will put the spacecraft into orbit around Mars, MOI-2 will transfer it toward Phobos, and MOI-3 will place it into its final orbit alongside the moon.Chris Philpot.

To reach Phobos, MMX will execute three major maneuvers: MOI-1 will put the spacecraft into orbit around Mars, MOI-2 will transfer it toward Phobos, and MOI-3 will place it into its final orbit alongside the moon.

It has been revealed that the best existing images of Phobos, from spacecraft such as NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter and ESA’s Mars Express, have resolutions of only a few meters per pixel. That’s larger than Idefix, the mission’s rover, itself about the size of a microwave oven. To map the surface in greater detail, MMX will loop in front of and behind Phobos at distances ranging from 200 kilometers to less than 20 km from the surface.

During its two-year remote sensing campaign, the exploration module will use several cameras and a laser altimeter to map the surface in high resolution and look for candidate landing sites. When Mars passes behind the Sun as seen from the Earth, causing a roughly two-week communications blackout, MMX will retreat into a larger, stable orbit. After communications resume, MMX will prepare to send its first visitor down to the surface.

According to recent reports, before the exploration and connected return modules attempt to land, Kawakatsu indicates, MMX will send a scout that in Japanese is called “the first penguin,” leaping into unknown waters. For this mission, the first to leap will be the Idefix rover, named for the canine companion to Obelix in the French comics series Asterix. The exploration module will release the rover during a low-altitude pass of between 40 and 100 meters above Phobos’s surface in 2028 or early 2029.

MMX will use its TENGOO camera [left] and LIDAR laser altimeter [right] to map Phobos’s terrain.JAXA.

It will be a tense moment that calls back to 2005, during Japan’s Hayabusa mission to explore the asteroid Itokawa. In a similarly designed drop, the MINERVA rover was released from an orbiter, but erroneously at 200 meters instead of the intended 70 meters. The rover missed the asteroid and, without propulsion, drifted off into deep space.

Idefix will get a slight nudge out of the exploration module toward its negligible-gravity target, freefalling and likely tumbling as it goes. It’s expected to touch down with a velocity of less than 1 meter per second. Unlike rovers that have landed on other surfaces with airbags or dedicated landing legs, Idefix will land without protection, apart from some extra padding on the solar panels due to their critical nature. The barely-there gravity of Phobos should allow the 23-kilogram rover to land softly, though exactly how this landing will play out is hard to predict.

The Idefix rover will travel to Phobos with its wheels tucked in and solar panels folded.DLR.

Sources indicate that “It will bounce probably several times,” says Stephan Ulamec, Idefix’s co-principal investigator and project manager at DLR. “It will come to rest somehow in some position.” Once it’s still, four retracted legs will deploy to right the rover autonomously, regardless of its orientation. It will then unfold its solar panels to charge its batteries for exploration tasks ahead.

A simulation shows how Idefix is expected to tumble onto Phobos, right itself using its articulated legs, and begin exploring the moon’s surface. DLR.

In a recent development, once operational, Idefix will roll at a snail’s pace, topping out at one millimeter per second. Its metal wheels have protruding blades like a paddle wheel, designed to gain traction in Phobos’s microgravity. “If we were to drive our rover faster, then it would actually be more like we were swimming through instead of driving across the surface,” claims Cecily Sunday, a doctoral student involved in testing Idefix’s WheelCams at the Institut Superieur de l’Aeronautique et de l’Espace (ISAE-Supaéro) in Toulouse, France.

The WheelCams, a pair of cameras placed on the underside of the rover, will observe the wheels and their tracks during Idefix’s planned 100-Earth-day primary mission. The images will help researchers study the size and distribution of grains in Phobos’s regolith and how cohesive they are. How much or how little the grains stick together will greatly impact how Idefix moves. Sunday likens this to the difference between driving on dry and wet sand. “Think of trying to build a sandcastle with dry sand,” she notes. “You can’t. Add water, and suddenly you can.”.

The Idefix rover was mounted between the MMX spacecraft’s landing legs for the journey to Phobos.DLR.

The team tested the rover’s nine-bladed wheels on a variety of materials, including Phobos regolith simulants provided by JAXA and DLR, lunar simulants, glass beads, quartz sand, and clay pebbles. “We characterize the mechanical properties of each simulant precisely, then test across the full range, with varying grain size, angularity, and even color, so we can map what we see in the WheelCam images back to actual surface properties,” Sunday says.

In a recent development, despite the microgravity and Phobos’s rubble-pile nature, Sunday says Earth-based tests can approximate the rover’s motion on the surface of the small moon fairly well. While Phobos’s reduced gravity lowers the rover’s effective weight, there is also reduced pressure between the grains beneath its wheels. “As long as you’re moving very, very slowly and using the same materials and the same weight of the system, they should be representative,” Sunday says.

With four paddle-like wheels and deployable solar panels, Idefix is designed to crawl across Phobos.Ardan Fuessmann/Imago/Alamy.

Idefix’s interactions with its new home will offer “sub-millimeter resolution and information on porosity, on grain size, on surface strength, on how hard is the material,” Ulamec says. “It fills a gap between remote observations from orbit and detailed observations of the return samples back on Earth.”.

What Idefix finds on this rocky, rugged world will help determine how and where JAXA attempts to land the main spacecraft. Michel notes the touchdown will provide ground truth for understanding of Phobos. When NASA’s OSIRIS-REx spacecraft touched down on the asteroid Bennu to collect a sample, its sampling arm surprisingly sank nearly half a meter into the loose material. But Ulamec doesn’t think Idefix will sink deep into Phobos, noting that Bennu is very different and much smaller, with a diameter of 500 meters.

According to recent reports, once Idefix has investigated the surface, MMX will face an even greater challenge: landing its much larger exploration module on Phobos. The spacecraft will make a controlled descent to roughly 10 meters above the surface, then drop the remaining distance in free fall. With so little gravity to pull it downward, even a small sideways motion could cause the lander to tip or bounce away. A successful, upright landing would mark the start of up to two hours on Phobos for the crucial sampling phase.

The MMX mission draws on the experience and technologies of Japan’s two Hayabusa sample-return missions, which landed on the asteroids Itokawa and Ryugu. But this mission has many more moving parts. MMX’s exploration module will use two sampling devices—a coring sampler developed by JAXA and a pneumatic sampler provided by NASA and fabricated by Honeybee Robotics, a subsidiary of Blue Origin. Data from these tools, and those carried by the Idefix rover, could answer questions about the origin of Phobos and how the Mars system has evolved.

The coring sampler uses a robot arm and a cylindrical corer designed to reach at least 2 centimeters below the surface. The arm can maneuver to find the best site for digging. “That by itself is a challenge because we’ve never done it,” Michel says. “You never know what can happen at the very sampling site itself, where you might have a boulder and the arm cannot move.”.

Probing beneath the top layer will be valuable because solar radiation, galactic cosmic rays, and micrometeorites have battered and weathered the surface. The material below should offer a better record of the moon’s origins, and JAXA aims to collect at least 10 grams of it.

MMX will carry both the Idefix rover [bottom] and a robotic coring sampler [top] designed to dig beneath Phobos’s weathered surface.JAXA.

According to recent reports, the pneumatic sampler takes a different approach. Mounted on one of the lander’s legs, it will inject pure, non-reactive nitrogen gas into the surface and capture the grains stirred up. This sample could illuminate the changes Mars and its moons have undergone over time. The dual system also adds redundancy in the face of Phobos’s unknowns. “If the surface of Phobos proves to be very hard, [the coring sampler] may struggle to penetrate the ground. [The pneumatic sampler] would not experience this issue and still be able to gather material,” Kawakatsu says.

One of the most intriguing aspects of MMX is the additional possibility of collecting material from the planet below. It’s likely that Phobos has been peppered by Martian ejecta thrown into space by meteor impacts, so MMX also provides an opportunity to return the first Martian samples to Earth. Michel estimates that the samples could contain “a few hundred grains coming from Mars.” Scientists can distinguish those grains from native Phobos material by analyzing their oxygen isotopes.

Sources indicate that that possibility raises a planetary-protection question. A direct Mars sample-return mission would have to follow strict rules to ensure that potentially living biological material from Mars doesn’t contaminate Earth. But those protocols don’t apply to MMX, even if its sample does collect grains of Martian soil. A panel of experts concluded that any microbes blasted off Mars wouldn’t survive the violent impact and ejection or the intense radiation exposure on the way to Phobos. This saved MMX from implementing expensive and time-consuming quarantine and containment protocols for the returning sample.

After landing on Phobos, MMX will have roughly two hours to collect samples from the moon’s surface before lifting off again.JAXA.

In a recent development, during the brief surface operation, the robotic arm will deposit the samples in a storage unit, from which they’ll be transferred into a capsule aboard the return module and sealed in a vacuum. After that, lift off.

Once back in Mars orbit, the exploration module will resume its observations of Phobos and make several flybys of Mars’s other diminutive moon, Deimos, to gather data on its surface, structure, and composition. In November 2030, during a favorable alignment of Mars and Earth, MMX will begin the homeward leg of its trip. The return module will separate from the exploration module and power the voyage home, its sole objective to bring the dust of Phobos to Earth.

MMX’s sample return capsule will carry material from Phobos through Earth’s atmosphere in 2031.JAXA.

Finally, in 2031, the 60-centimeter-wide sample capsule will plunge into Earth’s atmosphere at roughly 12 kilometers per second. Assuming it survives the extreme heat of reentry and lands safely in Australia, scientists will begin to tease out clues about Phobos and the early solar system. JAXA’s Institute of Space and Astronautical Science will receive and curate the samples, which will also be shared with mission partners.

It has been revealed that “We have macroscale measurements from the spacecraft, microscale measurements with the rover, and then sample analysis,” Michel indicates. “So we can relate the three kinds of scales together because we have all of them.” The insights gleaned from orbital images, close-up images of the regolith, and the chemical analysis of the samples could have wider implications for our understanding of our solar system.

Sources indicate that “MMX is a mission to understand the Mars system and shed light onto how terrestrial planets like the Earth, and maybe Mars, develop a habitable environment,” Kawakatsu notes. “We strongly suspect that our terrestrial planet region formed dry, and water and organics were scattered inwards from the icy-rich outer solar system.” Mars, he says, sits at the gateway between the inner and outer solar system, making its moons valuable witnesses to the processes that shaped potentially habitable worlds.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Meta employees have expressed concerns about what appear to be major privacy breaches when using Muse, at the moment the second most popular free iPhone app in the App Store with over 10 million downloads.

This includes again accessing end-to-end encrypted messaging without permission, and sharing what may be the bank balances of another Muse user ….

Siri AI was not the only AI app to launch back in September; Meta’s Muse AI app was debuted the same month, with the organization describing it as “your personal AI agent that gets things done across every part of life.”.

Recent findings suggest that muse initially debuted as an iPhone app, with Mac and iPad apps following shortly afterwards. It immediately moved to the top of the US App Store charts, overtaking ChatGPT. It rapidly exceeded 5 million downloads following a major advertising push by Meta, and that number has since doubled.

In a recent development, it wasn’t long before major privacy concerns were raised. Tech writer Jason Aten reported that the Mac app accessed his messages despite him explicitly refusing permission. The app then lied to him about how it had achieved this. Meta described this as a bug.

Security researcher Patrick Wardle also discovered a zero-day vulnerability that could allow an attacker to hijack dictated prompts, directing them instead to their own server.

I remarked at the time that I would absolutely not be one of the millions of people using the app, and the wisdom of that decision has now been underlined by a fresh report.

Sources indicate that reuters now reports Meta employees discussing further breaches. This includes another example of accessing encrypted messages without permission.

An employee using Muse on her personal phone reported it had surprised her with a reminder to respond to a message from her sister on Signal, an end-to-end encrypted messaging service popular with privacy advocates that competes with Meta’s WhatsApp.

“This seems like an extreme privacy violation. I definitely did not grant it access to other apps, or recall being asked about this,” the employee said in her post.

Industry observers note that the report notes this appears to have been done by capturing push notifications. However, this was what the app claimed had happened in the earlier case, and it turned out not to be true. The AI Now Institute was able to replicate the problem of Muse accessing Signal messages without permission.

Another employee reported receiving unsolicited bank balances that they say appeared to be those of another Muse user.

Muse had randomly added an extra message to its regular chats about fishing-related weather and tide information, saying: “BTW, two bank updates, your Capital One balance is $2722.58, your Charles Schwab balance is $5899.57.”.

“I have never shared my bank account with Muse and never discussed any banking topic with Muse. I’m afraid it’s sending other’s bank info to me,” the staffer wrote in his post.

Industry observers note that meta told Reuters that these were “isolated incidents” and suggested that the bank balances may have been AI hallucinations rather than leaked information. Update: Meta has now told us that the balances were definitely hallucinations.

"AI Agent" = Malware. There are an expanding number of "I told it not to do that" cases.

The instructions (prompt) you give the agent are a tiny fraction of the total prompt context the agent uses, and Meta/Grok/etc. is not going to let you see that context. Agents harvesting your data (ex. see full disk access) and sending it to the mothership is just another revenue/training stream. Even if you are paying you are still the product.

Meta has taken glitch with the messaging claims. It notes that access to either notifications or messaging must be explicitly granted.

With Android, people have the option to grant apps notification access, which allows apps to see notifications as they’re received. This is something users need to opt in to and is not specific to Muse. With Mac, to allow Muse to work on your behalf, you not only need to click allow for accessibility and screen recording, but after that it takes you to a settings screen where you once again need to confirm and turn this on.

The tech giant also implies that the experience of employees may relate to internal versions of Muse.

Employees have access to different versions of Muse than the public, so they’re often reviewing features, functionality, and behavior not available elsewhere.

I can only repeat my previous take on Muse: Nope.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, that last cut before winter is the trickiest mow of the year, and most lawn damage blamed on harsh winter weather actually starts with a badly timed final pass. Leave your grass too long and damp fall air turns it into a breeding ground for moss and snow mold, scalp it too short or mow over waterlogged turf, and the first hard freeze will weaken the roots until spring.

In a recent development, because shifting fall weather rarely follows a neat schedule, watching the calendar will only steer you wrong. Instead, your lawn gives away one clear visual sign when it is ready for winter, and knowing how to spot it, alongside a few simple mower adjustments, makes all the difference before the first freeze arrives.

It has been revealed that the surest signal it's time to pack the mower away is when your grass noticeably stops growing between cuts. Once the blades stay roughly the same height a week or two after a trim, your lawn has entered winter dormancy and no longer needs cutting.

Grass responds directly to soil and air temperatures, so most cool-season lawns continue putting on slow growth until daytime temperatures dip consistently below 50°F (and around 60°F for warm-season grasses).

As long as your turf is still actively growing, it benefits from occasional maintenance — but once temperatures drop and growth stalls, continuing to mow only stresses dormant blades that cannot repair themselves until spring.

In a recent development, when your grass is still putting on a little growth in late fall, a careful, well-timed trim sets it up to bounce back thicker and greener next year. Follow these four rules before storing your mower for the season:.

It has been revealed that never scalp the lawn for its final pass of the year. Set your mower to one of its highest settings, leaving the grass around 2 to 2.5 inches tall, so the blades have enough surface area to absorb winter sunlight while shielding the roots from freezing air.

Before making your final pass, rake or blow away thick layers of fallen leaves. Wet leaves block sunlight and smother the grass underneath, and running a mower straight over a heavy blanket of them clogs your deck and leaves soggy clumps behind.

According to recent reports, fall rain can leave lawns saturated for days at a time. Never mow wet grass or soggy soil, as heavy mower wheels compact the ground, tear out weakened roots, and leave muddy ruts that linger until spring. Wait for a dry, mild afternoon when the turf feels firm underfoot.

Industry observers note that even if your lawn looks a little shaggy, keep the mower in the shed whenever frost is on the ground or a hard freeze is in the forecast. Walking on or cutting frozen grass snaps the brittle blades, leaving brown, scorched patches that take months to recover.

Amazon’s Black Friday and Cyber Monday sale has officially started—but keeping track of the best discounts yet to land and figuring out which deals are worthwhile can be a challenge. As an alternative, you can have Alexa give you a heads-up about deals on products you already know you want to purchase, so you don’t have to spend time sorting through the noise.

Then head to the Alexa mobile app and go to More in the top left (the three horizontal lines) > Settings > Notifications > Amazon Shopping and toggle on Deal Recommendations under the Shopping Recommendations options. This ensures you’ll receive notifications for items that appear in your shopping activity.

Sources indicate that if Alexa finds an upcoming deal on something in your Saved for Later, your Wish List, or in your Shopping Cart, you’ll receive a pop-up alert on your Echo Show display or see a yellow light ring on your Echo speaker. You can also ask, “Alexa, what are my notifications?” to hear a list of deals it has compiled thus far. You can also say "Alexa, let me know when [product name] goes on sale.".

Alexa can detect deals up to 24 hours in advance, so you can either ask it to remind you again when a deal starts or request that it buy the item when the deal goes live. Simply say, “Alexa, buy it for me,” and it’ll charge the default payment and send the item to the default delivery address on your account.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In light of growing pushback from users who want more control over how AI is integrated into their apps (if at all), Canva is introducing newly introduced settings that let them hide generative AI features and see less AI-generated content.
  • Canva today announced new controls that will let Free and Pro people choose whether to see generative AI features across the app, as well as how much AI-generated content appears in search results and in recommendations for templates and design elements.
  • The organization notes that both controls are available at no additional cost and can be turned on or off at any time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In light of growing pushback from users who want more control over how AI is integrated into their apps (if at all), Canva is introducing newly introduced settings that let them hide generative AI features and see less AI-generated content. Here are the details.

Canva today announced new controls that will let Free and Pro people choose whether to see generative AI features across the app, as well as how much AI-generated content appears in search results and in recommendations for templates and design elements.

The organization notes that both controls are available at no additional cost and can be turned on or off at any time.

According to Canva, “the future of creativity isn’t a choice between AI and no AI.” For this reason, it is introducing the following controls:.

The company says that, while it knows that there is an ongoing debate between customers with opposing views on whether AI has a place in creative work, it thinks “both views are valid”:.

“It’s not our place to tell anyone how to create, so today we’re launching two new controls that put that decision firmly with our community […].”.

Importantly, the company noted that select features that use AI without generating upcoming content will remain available even when generative AI features are turned off:.

Industry observers note that “Some of Canva’s everyday editing tools use AI to make simple tasks faster, without generating anything new. Background Remover, one of Canva’s most popular tools, lifts a subject cleanly out of a photo in a single click, and Magic Grab lets creators select an object in an image and move it somewhere else in the design. Both remain available when the generative AI switch is off, because they work only with what’s already in a design.”.

Canva added that these tools also won’t add an AI label to a design’s metadata, since that label is reserved for AI-generated content.

As for the manufacturer’s design content library, Canva said that while “a small portion of the library is AI-generated content made by Canva, including some abstract backgrounds and illustrated graphics,” its community has told it “they want an easier way to find design assets made by real people, so the content control reduces the number of AI-generated templates and elements that appear in search results and recommendations.”.

With today’s announcement, Canva is essentially expanding on the AI permissions already available to administrators of Business, Enterprise, Teams, and Education accounts, which let organizations control how their teams use AI.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Watermelon Pictures and the Film Committee at Media City Qatar have announced a planned strategic partnership to develop and co-produce a slate of films telling stories from the Global South.

For Watermelon, the partnership marks a significant expansion into larger-scale, mainstream production.

Badie Ali and Hamza Ali released their Chicago-based production and distribution tech giant in 2024, with a mission to amplify Palestinian and other under-represented voices.

In a recent development, until now, the tech giant has focused mainly on distribution, with recent releases including The Voice of Hind Rajab, El Sett, Who Killed Alex Odeh? and American Doctor. Related Stories News Egyptian Music Star Mohamed Mounir Gets Biopic - Doha Industry Days News 'Al Hayba' Star Taim Hasan To Play Syrian Whistleblower Farid Al-Madhhan In Neon-Backed 'Caesar' Biopic.

Sources indicate that its cofounders recently signaled to Deadline that they were working on a development slate, without going into detail. Watch on Deadline.

The strategic partnership aims to combine Qatar’s infrastructure and resources as it seeks to grow the film and TV sector at home and regionally, and Watermelon’s access to leading talent, established distribution infrastructure, and understanding of what resonates with audiences.

“When we founded Watermelon Pictures, our vision was to bring powerful stories to the big screen with an unwavering commitment to authenticity,” said Watermelon Pictures cofounder Badie Ali.

“Our partnership with the Film Committee at Media City Qatar is a major step toward realizing that promise, allowing us to tell these stories on a larger scale while remaining true to the people and places at their heart.”.

Under the partnership, the parties would aim to shoot projects substantially in Qatar or structure them as Qatari co-productions.

They would also seek to involve Doha-based post-production companies and help eligible projects access the Qatar Screen Production Incentive (QSPI), creating opportunities for local crews, businesses, and creative talent while strengthening Qatar’s position as an international production hub.

Sources indicate that “Through this partnership, we want to give filmmakers the resources to tell stories rooted in their communities and bring them to audiences around the world. We also want the films we support to create work for crews and businesses in Qatar and give them experience they can carry into their next production,” noted Hassan Al Thawadi, Chairman of the Film Committee at Media City Qatar.

In a recent development, the Film Committee and Watermelon Pictures will jointly identify projects for the initial slate. The proposed partnership is subject to definitive agreements and the required approvals, with projects to be considered individually. More details on specific projects are soon to be confirmed.

“Too many compelling stories and perspectives, including those of Arab and Muslim communities, have historically been underrepresented in mainstream cinema. We see an enormous opportunity to change that. Our planned slate will span genres, challenge perceptions, and, above all, entertain. Our ambition isn’t simply to create space in the industry. It’s to compete at its highest level,” said Watermelon Pictures cofounder Hamza Ali.

The announcement of the planned partnership was made during the Film Committee’s Doha Industry Days, running from November 19 to 21 within the framework of the Doha Film Festival.

While the Nintendo Switch 2 has surged to prominence again, the Steam Deck and other handheld PCs of its ilk have shown there’s huge demand for consoles that let you take your Steam (and other launcher) libraries on the go.

One of our most pleasantly surprising entrants in this field, the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+. It's one of the best you can find, but it would be fair to say its price tag put a few folks off. Now, thanks to a handy voucher code at Very (valid until tomorrow!), you can save £300 off the sticker price.

Use voucher code FLASH20 for 20% off, which brings the price down to £1199.

In a recent development, the code you’ll need to apply at checkout is FLASH20, and it’s not just limited to gaming handhelds. In fact, it applies to selected Copilot+, laptops, and PCs.

Sources indicate that if you’re just using it here, though, you’re unlikely to be disappointed. My colleague Jason England reviewed the Claw 8 EX AI+ at launch and found its only real drawback to be the price. In fact, he even dubbed it the “best PC gaming handheld” he’d tested, awarding it four stars out of five.

The MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ has the Intel Arc G3 chip driving things under the hood, which is essentially a supercharged chip that offers impressive performance while not instantly draining the battery the moment you attempt to play something more demanding.

It’s also packing 32GB of RAM (which is probably a good reason the price is as high as it is, given the ongoing RAM crisis) and 1TB of storage, as well as a microSD card slot. It has a unique “chin” to the display (more on that in a moment) that actually helps with ergonomics, and there’s improved button feel and haptics over MSI’s prior models.

Recent findings suggest that while we’d have loved OLED (especially at this price point), the IPS panel here has a variable refresh rate for smoother gameplay, and 8-inches, is actually big enough to get some work done in a pinch with a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse combo. In fact, because it’s running Windows 11, you also get the Xbox Full Screen Experience for a more console-like experience: The best of both worlds.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you’re going to commit to an Amazon Prime membership, you might as well squeeze as much as you can out of the deal. And there's a good amount of juice to squeeze there. The price you pay for Amazon depends on many factors, but regardless of how much you're paying, it's worth it for most people (we've done the math).

Sources indicate that if you're on the fence about signing up, consider that Amazon's Black Friday and Cyber Monday sale is underway, and the manufacturer is hosting some amazing tech deals. It's a great time to sell your soul—or take advantage of the 30-day free trial—and there's a lot more to your membership than just deals and free shipping.

According to recent reports, the standard Prime membership costs $14.99 per month or $139 per year, but there are other tiers that some people might qualify for. For example, the Amazon Prime for Young Adults program allows young adults between the ages of 18 and 24 to get all of the Prime perks for half the cost—$7.49 per month or $69 annually.

I'll be the first to admit I didn't know all of the benefits that Amazon Prime offers to its members. There are a lot more perks than people think. Here are the most impressive ones (and check out the full list):.

Fast free shipping on millions of items: Depending on where you live, shipping can take one or two days, and some even come on the same day for orders of $25 or more in most areas—and it’s always free (if being shipped by the Amazon store).

Select pre-ordered items can be delivered on their release date for free (for most areas).

The option to have items delivered inside your garage with a smart garage device (depending on where you live) for $1.99 per order, or for free if you combine it with Amazon Day delivery.

Earn rewards for future purchases when you select free no-rush shipping.

The option to have all your weekly orders delivered on a specific day, to reduce waste from boxes.

Industry observers note that amazon Prime Visa card: Cardholders get 5% back on Amazon, Whole Foods, Chase Travel, and other purchases. Prime members who use this card extensively can earn rewards that offset the cost of membership.

Recent findings suggest that A Grubhub+ and Uber Eats membership, normally $9.99 per month, which gets you free delivery on eligible orders, lower service fees, exclusive deals, and other perks as long as you remain a Prime Member (it used to be only for a year). The Uber Eats membership gets you free delivery on eligible restaurants of $25 or more.

Recent findings suggest that sharing with family or friends: Amazon Family is the existing program for sharing Prime benefits, and it allows you to add separate profiles for one other adult who lives in the same household as the primary account holder, up to four teens, and up to four child accounts. This grants access to all the standard benefits, such as free delivery, Prime Video with ads, Prime Reading, third-party benefits like Grubhub, and access to audiobooks, e-books, certain games, and Amazon Music.

Sources indicate that amazon Health: Prime people get One Medical access for an additional $9 per month or $99 per year. Through your devices, you’ll have 24/7 access to on-demand virtual care, plus real-life access to primary care offices in a number of U.S. cities. It accepts most major health insurance looks, too.

Amazon Pharmacy: Access to free two-day delivery and other savings on medications.

Prime Video: Prime includes unlimited streaming of movies, TV demonstrates, and Amazon Originals with ads, which normally costs $9 per month.

Amazon Music Prime: Access to Amazon's Spotify-esque music streaming service (not to be confused with Amazon's other music streaming subscriptions).

Amazon Luna: A cloud gaming platform that offers newly introduced free games every month, free downloadable PC games, content, a monthly Twitch channel subscription, and a free channel subscription on Twitch each month for Prime Members.

Amazon Photos: Unlimited photo storage plus 5 GBs for videos and other files (which extends to members of your Family Vault).

Prime Reading: Free access to a rotating selection of e-books and magazines for Kindle or Fire tablets and Kindle apps.

Amazon's First Reads: You get up to two free e-books every month from a curated list of books handpicked by editors.

Unlike Sony’s recent theatrical release of The Social Reckoning, which arguably didn’t resonate with the current tech era we’re living in, Neon is unwrapping Luca Guadagnino‘s Artificial about Open AI co-founders Sam Altman, Ilya Sutskever and Elon Musk at a time when we fear the technology will end us.

Now whether that’s in regards to our existence or our financial livelihoods is another question.

Sources indicate that earlier this week, former OpenAI alum and Altman rival Dario Amodei’s Anthropic went public creating a $1.18 trillion company. However, shares fell from its $111 day-of-market price to $88.91 EOD Friday. Neon is shrewdly opening Artificial limited on Christmas Day (the perfect time to launch a sophisticated adult skewing awards contender), and in the run-up to that release, following premieres at New York Film Festival and BFI London Film Fest, along with current awards voter screenings, anticipation is boiling for the pic evident in its current 95% fresh Rotten Tomatoes critics rating. Related Stories News Timothée Chalamet Addresses Possibility Of A 'Call Me by Your Name' Sequel: "Never Say Never" News Sam Altman On 'Artificial' Movie About Him -- Not Among "Ten Weirdest Things In My Life" Right Now.

Sources indicate that as a filmmaker who knows something about love with the Zendaya starring tennis love triangle pic, Challengers, and Oscar winning gay romance, Call Me By Your Name, we spoke with Guadagnino on the latest Crew Call as to what pulled him into the OpenAI-verse. Watch on Deadline.

Recent findings suggest that take a listen below. Essentially, it’s about about a bunch of young mad, narcissistic scientists acting like flawed Greek Gods in San Francisco:.

Well before its theatrical release, Artificial generated a lot of controversy as its original studio, Amazon MGM Studios, backed away from the movie out of fear of OpenAI. That’s because Amazon has a $50 billion investment in the Altman non-profit.

According to recent reports, however, unlike the Facebook camp back when Social Network was getting released in 2010, there’s been zero ill will coming from Altman or OpenAI about Guadaganino’s film. In fact, you could say they’re great sports.

In a sit-down with the Vanity Fair podcast, Altman states he “did not” coerce Amazon to drop Artificial. “I don’t know anyone else who did,” he added, “I didn’t speak to Jeff Bezos.”.

In fact, Guadagnino brazenly shot the pic outside Altman’s house in San Francisco. The filmmaker tells us about that. For Altman, he was giddy about running into his onscreen doppelgänger, Andrew Garfield: “One morning, I was walking down the street to get coffee and there were all these cameras and there was a guy dressed exactly like me with the same backpack, walking so much, I felt like I was in a weird glitch or a simulation.”.

Altman emphasized to Vanity Fair that Garfield “did walk like me.”.

It has been revealed that while Altman hasn’t seen Artificial, his reaction to the trailer is, “I don’t think they’re going for accuracy, so in that sense it doesn’t bother me. They’re trying to make a good movie and maybe it will be good. It won’t be good as an accurate depiction, except for the walk. I’m sure they’ll get other parts right at least accidentally.”.

One of the jaw dropping moments shown in the Artificial trailer is Altman having a bunker in his wine country estate loaded with guns.

“That is an example of an inaccuracy,” Altman told Vanity Fair, “There’s no bunker with firearms on the wall.”.

“I have a survivalist mindset,” Altman admitted, “but I don’t have a setup that is depicted in that trailer.”.

Guadagnino tells Deadline, “I have validated the validating information that has been vetted: He does have guns.”.

In a recent development, while the filmmaker experienced zero pushback from OpenAI and Altman during production on the Simon Rich script, he claims “We were very careful that everything that was in the movie had to be approved legally, so that we were not bending facts and reality for our narrative purposes. But, because the truth in this case is more extraordinary than any fiction, that was okay. Because we had the drama, we had the juice.”.

When it came to Amazon exiting Artificial, Guadagnino had a Zen mindset: “I was cool because I like disruptions, very much.”.

“Their decision to give the movie to us to find another home was truly honorable, because they could have written off the movie and (noted) ‘Bye-bye’.”.

As far as Artificial being a hot potato that no studio wanted to handle, except NEON, Guadagnino asserts that “All the speculation about nobody wanting the movie; I like to think that there was the need (by the media) to fill blank pages with nothing.”.

Industry observers note that for off the bat, per Guadagnino, NEON was first, front and center in their passion to takeover the project after CAA screened it for them. Listen above for more details.

When it comes to the paranoia out there that AI is the catalyst for human extinction in ten years, the filmmaker tells Deadline, “I don’t have trust and I don’t have faith in humans.”.

His suspicions about AI stem from growing up during the Cold War. “I remember very well in 1985 when Chernobyl happened,” he adds.

And there’s myriad reasons for concerns about AI, from a Chatbot being at the center of 16-year old Adam Raine’s suicide, to AI trespassing and impostering another firm’s security space.

We also talk with the Call Me By Your Name Best Picture Oscar nominee on why Andrew Garfield was the right guy to play Altman, and the Open AI Boss’ sincerity when it comes to creating guardrails for the technology.

  • IEEE Spectrum Magazine, the flagship publication of the IEEE, explores the development, applications and implications of new technologies.

Electronic products now pack circuits, structures, thermal paths, and packaging into very small spaces. These physical domains interact with one another. A packaging choice can change how a shock load reaches a circuit board. Such interactions are hard to predict. Most are found during physical qualification, late in development. At that stage, the design is mostly fixed. A failure leads to redesign, rebuilds, and retesting. Physical tests give strong evidence of robustness, but they give limited insight into load paths and failure margins. Traditional simulation gives more detail, but it needs specialist skills and long manual setup. This white paper explains how guided virtual validation brings shock and drop assessment into the design phase. It reviews common test configurations, model inputs, and acceptance criteria. A packaged drop case study then highlights how packaging can be optimized across all drop orientations and checked against physical test results.

We've had the privilege to test all four mattresses, and here's what we think of each one in terms of value for money, sleep needs, and support for different body types...

Sources indicate that if saving money is your top priority when looking for a king mattress, then the Nectar Classic is our top recommendation. At $899 for a king mattress, the mid-range Nectar Classic is the cheapest option of the four and one of the best mattresses under $1,000. Plus, it comes with unbeatable benefits, including a year-long sleep trial and a lifetime warranty.

According to recent reports, another good mid-range choice is the Casper One, which is under $1,150. However, the benefits (including a 10-year warranty and a 100-night sleep trial) are decent but average. The Purple Plus and the Tempur-Adapt, meanwhile, are in the same price tier as the best luxury mattresses.

Sources indicate that while Nectar doesn't provide a specific weight limit, they claim that its beds are engineered to accommodate various body types. Likewise, Tempur-Pedic says its mattresses do not have a weight limit either. According to the brand, Casper mattresses "are designed to support all shapes and sizes.".

As for Purple mattresses' weight capacity, its king size beds can support at least 500 pounds and are tested to support 700 pounds of total weight, making them suitable for a wide range of body weights.

While none of the mattresses above are designed specifically for heavier bodies, there are plenty of mattresses designed for plus-sized sleepers. For instance, the WinkBed Plus is built to support sleepers and couples who weigh over 250lbs.

As all our top picks here are made entirely of foam layers, each one displayed excellent motion isolation in our tests, which means you won't feel your partner's wriggling travelling over to your side of the bed. As for temperature regulation, our testers found that the Purple Plus's ventilated design sleeps incredibly cool if you or your partner tend to overheat.

If you find yourself sleeping close to the edge of your bed because of a partner who likes to stretch out and hog most of the mattress, then the Nectar Classic is a great option as it showcased strong edge support in our at-home and lab-based tests. Its edge are sturdy and won't make you feel as if you're going to roll out of bed when sleeping near the sides.

Recent findings suggest that in terms of comfort, the Nectar Classic and the Casper One offer firm support to back and stomach sleepers, while the Tempur-Adapt is best for back sleeping. As for side sleepers who need plusher pressure relief, the Purple Plus offers both support for back and front sleepers and body-contouring comfort for side sleepers.

#62624. These 14 New Features Are Coming to iOS 27.3

📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

These 14 New Features Are Coming to iOS 27.3

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1477 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, apple has been beta testing iOS 27.3 since Nov.
  • In a recent development, technically, anyone with a compatible iPhone can try out iOS 27.3 right now—assuming you enroll your Apple Account in the developer program.
  • The iPhone Duo is Apple's first foldable smartphone, but also the company's first phone since the iPhone SE 3 to ship with Touch ID.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, apple has been beta testing iOS 27.3 since Nov. 3. While this update isn't as large as iOS 27 proper, it's surprisingly feature-filled for a 0.3 update. This is only a beta, so anything could (and likely will) change before Apple officially launches the update. But, as it stands, iOS 27.3 tests 10 newly introduced features—including one feature the company trialed in the previous beta.

In a recent development, technically, anyone with a compatible iPhone can try out iOS 27.3 right now—assuming you enroll your Apple Account in the developer program. But a word of warning: Betas can be temperamental, and could be risky. As such, I'd recommend avoiding the beta until Apple releases the public beta, which comes after a bit more testing to iron out larger issues. Either way, make sure to make a full backup of your iPhone to a Mac or PC first, as issues with the beta could result in permanent data loss.

The iPhone Duo is Apple's first foldable smartphone, but also the company's first phone since the iPhone SE 3 to ship with Touch ID. While it works well enough for unlocking your iPhone, it's still an adjustment for those of us used to Face ID. With iOS 27.3, Apple is now testing face unlock for the Duo—not Face ID, mind you. The Duo's front camera doesn't have the tech required to power Face ID or its secure protocols. Instead, this feature simply unlocks your iPhone Duo with a face scan. In addition, your Duo will still require Touch ID for Apple Pay and passwords, or after 45 minutes of inactivity. You can read more about this upcoming feature here.

iOS 27.3 also comes with a latest setting that lets you lock your iPhone Duo by closing it—as you would expect from, say, a laptop—or, dare I say, a flip phone? Currently, closing the Duo seamlessly transitions what's on the big screen to the smaller display, and you have to press the side button to lock the phone.

With watchOS 27, Apple released "Audio Intelligence," a latest set of features for Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. Audio Intelligence uses the watches' new S11 chip, along with on-device AI and cloud-based AI, to run new features, like Sound Recognition and Shazam (music recognition).

According to recent reports, with iOS 27.3, however, the firm is now officially testing the other two Audio Intelligence features it originally unveiled with watchOS 27. First, there's Live Rewind: By double-clicking the watch crown, you can pull up a transcript of the last 15 seconds of a conversation. Siri Recap, on the other hand, displays summaries of conversations you had that day, in case you need a refresher on any chats you might have otherwise forgotten about,.

Sources indicate that the firm generated some controversy when it first revealed these two Audio Intelligence features, since, on the surface, it sounds like these newly introduced Apple Watches are essentially spying on people all day long. According to Apple, however, that isn't really the case. The company claims Audio Intelligence is private, and never records or stores any audio. No speakers are ever identified, and text results (both transcripts and summaries) are deleted automatically after a set period of time unless the user saves them to the Siri app. You can read more about how Audio Intelligence works here.

It has been revealed that despite their claims, I'm sure there will still be strong feelings surrounding these Audio Intelligence features. We'll have to see whether Apple can prove Live Rewind and Siri Recap aren't all that creepy throughout the iOS 27.3 beta process.

Recent findings suggest that iOS 27.3 also introduces app actions for Siri AI. Apple is testing newly introduced abilities for Siri AI, including organizing files, planning events, or adding photos to albums. You could ask Siri to organize your Downloads folder, or delete files that haven't been opened in more than a year. You could ask Siri to find a coffee shop you went to last week, or to save an article to your Reading List in Safari. You could ask Siri to check your calendar and set up a time for an event based on when you're free. You can even ask the assistant to schedule, edit, or unsend messages.

For example, you could ask Siri AI to help you initiative a trip with your friends. You could ask the AI to put together a themed playlist in Apple Music, schedule a message to a group about an upcoming trip, organize the websites you've been visiting in Safari into a tab group, and, after the trip, ask Siri to move your best photos to your favorites album. These upcoming actions work in the following apps: Calendar, Files, Finder, Journal, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Notes, Photos, Preview, Reminders, Safari, Shortcuts, and Weather. Developers can also add Siri AI app actions support to their own apps.

Apple started testing its upcoming Health app with the iOS 27.2 beta, but pulled the redesign before the official release. Now, with iOS 27.3, the new app is back. The new Health app has a health dashboard for the first time, as well as new features like Health Age and movement assessments. It seems to be pulling from some popular competitor services, hopefully, for the better. For more on the new Health app, check out Lifehacker health editor Beth Skwarecki's explainer.

It has been revealed that continuing on the Health track, iOS 27.3 also introduces "Gym Strength." This is a newly introduced Fitness+ feature that offers a personalized four-week strength-training plan. You can customize these plans to meet your goals, experience level, and schedule, and they adapt as you progress. You'll get recommendations based on your experience with exercises, reps, and sets, including video demos for exercises. You can access Gym Strength on both iPhone and iPad, and Apple Watches are optional—though you can log your progress with the wearable if you have it.

Recent findings suggest that apple is also testing a new Siri AI feature in Safari, that gives the bot access to entire webpages, including the parts of the site that aren't on-screen. Say you want to know all the gluten-free options on a menu on a restaurant's website, but only a portion of the site is actually in view. You could ask Siri to read you the gluten-free options, and it would pull from the whole page, even though you can only see part of it.

Vertical tabs have been a favorite among browser aficionados, as they give you more screen real estate in your browser while keeping your tabs off the side. Apple hasn't made the jump—until now. This feature works with iPads running iPadOS 27.3 as well as Macs running macOS 27.3.

It has been revealed that another upcoming Safari feature in testing is "Adaptive Dark Mode." This feature forces websites into a dark theme, if they don't have a native theme of their own. There are third-party apps that can do this, but this is the first time Apple has offered this feature built into Safari.

Apple is also testing fresh StandBy experiences with iOS 27.3, which were previously only available on the iPhone Duo. When you turn your iPhone sideways while plugged in, you'll find new Analog and Digital Clock faces with new customization options. There's also a new Photos face, with the option to pull images from Shared Albums.

"Reachability" pulls your iPhone's display down towards the bottom of the screen, so you can access items towards the top of the display with one hand. It's a useful feature for those of us with big iPhones, and now, there's no iPhone bigger than the Duo. With iOS 27.3, Apple is testing Reachability for its first foldable phone. It's a bit like the inverse of how Reachability currently works: You can swipe on the left or right side of your Duo's display to shift the other side of the screen towards your current position. If you're holding your Duo in your left hand, a swipe of the left side will pull the right side over to the left, and vice versa.

Apple is also rolling out upcoming languages for Siri AI in iOS 27.3. Now, Apple's smart assistant supports Traditional Chinese, Vietnamese, Turkish, and Norwegian.

If you have an Apple Intelligence-compatible iPad running iPadOS 27.3, you now have access to Siri Mode in Camera. As with iOS, you can open the Camera app on iPadOS to access Siri Mode, and ask Siri about your surroundings.

If you watch videos in Apple Podcasts, you can find them in more sources than the Podcasts app. With the new updates, you'll find these videos on Apple TV 4K, select smart TVs, your iPhone, iPad, Mac, and even in CarPlay. (Please don't watch video podcasts while driving.).

UK court rules Apple can share the top secret order everyone already knew

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (762 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Investigatory Powers Tribunal – essentially a British court that deals with complaints about state surveillance – has ruled that Apple is allowed to reveal a secret order it received from the UK government.
  • Apple had already found a clever way to alert British customers to the classified order without breaking the law, but it can now confirm what we all already knew, and talk openly about the matter ….
  • The story centers on Apple’s introduction of the Advanced Data Protection (ADP) privacy feature back in 2022.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Investigatory Powers Tribunal – essentially a British court that deals with complaints about state surveillance – has ruled that Apple is allowed to reveal a secret order it received from the UK government.

Apple had already found a clever way to alert British customers to the classified order without breaking the law, but it can now confirm what we all already knew, and talk openly about the matter ….

The story centers on Apple’s introduction of the Advanced Data Protection (ADP) privacy feature back in 2022. This extended end-to-end encryption to almost all your iCloud data, meaning Apple has no access, and therefore cannot grant access to any government agencies who come knocking on its door.

Recent findings suggest that the feature is off by default because it means Apple cannot help you access any of your data if, for example, you forget your iCloud password. However, those who want to maximize the privacy of their iCloud account can enable it.

Industry observers note that in 2025, the British government ordered Apple to create a backdoor to allow access by security services and law enforcement. Even worse, the order was issued under legislation that prohibits companies from revealing that they have received this demand.

According to recent reports, this would have meant that British customers who enabled ADP would think that their data was safe when in fact it wasn’t. As we’ve mentioned many times before, any backdoor created for use by the good guys is vulnerable to discovery and exploitation by the bad guys.

It would have been illegal for Apple to reveal that it had been instructed to compromise the privacy of customer data, but the organization found a clever way to effectively communicate this without breaking the law. Apple announced it was withdrawing ADP from the UK without explaining its reason.

In a recent development, “Apple can no longer offer Advanced Data Protection (ADP) in the United Kingdom to newly introduced consumers and current UK users will eventually need to disable this security feature. ADP protects iCloud data with end-to-end encryption, which means the data can only be decrypted by the user who owns it, and only on their trusted devices. We are gravely disappointed that the protections provided by ADP will not be available to our customers in the UK […] As we have said many times before, we have never built a backdoor or master key to any of our products or services and we never will.”.

Tell me you’ve been ordered to create a backdoor to ADP without telling me you’ve been ordered to create a backdoor to ADP ….

At this point, it was an open secret. However, ridiculously, despite the fact that everyone in the security and privacy field knew about it and was talking about it, Apple was still not allowed to officially confirm it.

Sources indicate that the iPhone maker asked the Investigatory Powers Tribunal (IPT) to allow it to openly discuss the order, with privacy campaigners backing this call. The Financial Times reports that the court has now ruled in Apple’s favor.

The UK government must admit that it issued a secret order to Apple to allow it access to encrypted customer data, a court has ruled […] The Home Office has “not established that it would be damaging to national security” to reveal that Apple had received a “technical capability notice” (TCN), the tribunal mentioned. The ruling means that […] “much” of Apple and the non-profits’ legal challenge can now take place in open court.

One of the great ironies is that most people had never heard of ADP until the government effectively made it headline news in the tech press three years after it rolled out – a classic example of the Streisand Effect.

Sources indicate that this ruling is a win both for transparency and commonsense. To be clear, the actual requirement for a backdoor remains in place, but this can now be challenged in open court.

Pairing with an iPhone or iPad running the iOS or iPadOS 27.3 beta may cause Siri requests to fail.

According to recent reports, it’s unknown how many reports of Siri concerns on HomeView can be attributed to the iOS 27.3 beta. However, it wouldn’t surprise me if many of the reports were from beta users. That’s in part because early HomeView reviewers didn’t seem to have the same problems.

Sources indicate that with HomeView 27.2.1 now available, those problems should hopefully be taken care of. However, if you’re on the iOS 27.3 beta, there’s a fresh matter you’ll need to deal with temporarily.

As discovered by pdfu, if you try to make a Personal Content request on an iPhone running iOS 27.3, Siri in HomeView 27.2.1 now says: “I can’t help with that because your personal device is on newer software.”.

In a recent development, if you’re on iOS 27.3, Siri on HomeView can’t use your iPhone for personal context, likely until December.HomeView won’t send Siri requests to an iPhone on newer software. Without a HomeView enhancement, your only option is iOS 27.2.x.On-device requests like timers still work. https://t.co/8UbRs7z496.

It’s understandable that issues might arise from having iOS and HomeView software that’s out of sync. Unfortunately though, there’s no beta software available for HomeView at the moment.

That means unless Apple releases a beta soon, people might have to wait until the public launch of HomeView 27.3 in December to get Personal Content features back.

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that microsoft is saying goodbye to its task management service To Do, including the Mac and iOS apps.
  • Sources indicate that the last day to use the To Do apps is June 30, 2027.
  • “Microsoft To Do is retiring,” Microsoft explains.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that microsoft is saying goodbye to its task management service To Do, including the Mac and iOS apps. Here’s what owners need to know.

Sources indicate that the last day to use the To Do apps is June 30, 2027. That date also applies to Windows, Android, and the web. The underlying service and sync support will retire later, according to Microsoft’s support document.

“Microsoft To Do is retiring,” Microsoft explains. “For work or school accounts, Microsoft Planner will be the destination for managing personal work tasks alongside assigned work. The updated My tasks experience begins rolling out in December 2026.”.

It has been revealed that on the Mac, you can use Planner on the web or in Teams. Microsoft explicitly claims it has no intends for a native Mac app.

You can still see your existing To Do tasks in Planner through June 30, but your tasks and lists won’t carry over. Microsoft plans to offer an export option before the apps retire.

It has been revealed that planner doesn’t support personal Microsoft accounts however. If that’s how you use To Do, you’ll need to pick another task manager, even if you pay for Microsoft 365 Personal or Family, according to the firm.

Industry observers note that the June shutdown will end a run of just over a decade for To Do on Apple platforms. Microsoft bought the organization behind Wunderlist in 2015 and released the first iPhone preview of To Do in April 2017.

Looking for a proper replacement? Apple’s built-in Reminders app can keep lists in sync between Apple devices, including a grocery list you share with family through iCloud.

Industry observers note that microsoft has been trying to make Teams as the super app for some time now, as Planner is integrated into Teams. Teams is one of the prime examples of why super apps are terrible, with a bloated, web app-like experience.

If you liked To Do because it worked across platforms, Todoist has apps for iPhone, iPad, Mac, Windows, and Android.

Industry observers note that does this sunsetting affect you? Were you a Wunderlist user back in the day? Share your thoughts in the comments.

Update: Howard Crow, Director of Product, Agents and AI, Microsoft, shared this statement with 9to5Mac regarding the transition:.

It has been revealed that “We’re bringing task management experiences together across Microsoft 365 to make it easier for customers to manage individual tasks and team plans. As part of this transition, Microsoft To Do apps will retire on June 30, 2027, with work and school experiences coming together in Microsoft Planner. Existing integrations across Microsoft 365, including Outlook and Teams, will also be updated to work with Planner. We recognize this change will affect customers differently, particularly those using personal Microsoft accounts, and we’re committed to helping them prepare. Customers will be able to export their To Do data before retirement, and we’ll share additional guidance to support the transition.”.

If you’re hunting for deals on Asics running shoes this Black Friday, you’re going to have to settle for buying last-gen models right now, because I’ve yet to see any notable discounts on the latest sneakers.

Recent findings suggest that however, this is no bad thing. I often recommend buying the previous model of popular shoes in general, because brands frequently only make minor updates to the latest version so you get better value on last-gen sneakers in sales.

That’s definitely the case with several top Asics shoes right now, and having tested both the latest and past models of popular picks like the Novablast, Gel-Nimbus and Gel-Kayano I can tell you what you are — and aren’t — missing out on by getting an older shoe.

The Sonicblast is not one of Asics' better-known shoes, but flying under the radar means that it's one of the most heavily-discounted right now. It's a plated trainer with a firm, fast ride that's good for workouts or races, and best paired with a more comfortable option like the Gel-Nimbus in a running shoe rotation.

The Cumulus sits below the Nimbus in the Asics line-up as a more affordable cushioned daily trainer, and I think the Gel-Nimbus 27 is better value than the Gel-NImbus 28 in the sales right now thanks to this deal. It has a smooth ride and is comfortable for long runs, and the newer Gel-Cumulus 28 isn't a major upgrade based on my testing.

In a recent development, the Gel-Kayano is Asics' premium stability running shoe, offering a little more support for overpronators on the run than the Gel-Nimbus 28. I've been testing the Kayano for many years and while there have been some changes made with the Asics Gel-Kayano 33, I rate the Gel-Kayano 32 the better buy thanks to this deal.

According to recent reports, I keep hoping to see the Novablast 5 drop cheaper than this in the sales, but so far it's stuck firmly at $129, which is no doubt a sign of its popularity. I rate the Novablast as the best Asics cushioned shoe myself, because it's lighter and livelier than the Nimbus and Cumulus. While the Asics Novablast 6 is an excellent update the Novablast 5 remains a great daily trainer worth considering at this lower price.

Recent findings suggest that I'm right now testing the Asics Gel-Nimbus 29, which has a very different feel to the 28 thanks to a softer midsole foam. Many will prefer the fresh shoe for this, but it actually strays into the 'too soft' category for me, sapping the energy at times during runs. If you don't want to take that risk, the Gel-Nimbus 28 is a reliable cushioned cruiser that's reduced by $40 in the sales.

The Asics Superblast 3 is one of the better running shoes I've tested this year, but I'd still eye up this deal on the Superblast 2 in the sales if you're looking for a versatile max-cushioned sneaker. It's great for all kinds of runs, and I often used the Superblast 2 for trips with a lot of walking as well.

iOS 27 gave AirPods Pro a variety of upcoming features, but there’s another addition that’s easy to miss: a convenient new setting in Control Center for Adaptive Audio.

Several AirPods models offer excellent Active Noise Cancellation and Transparency modes—especially AirPods Pro 3 (now only $179).

But Adaptive Audio is another option you may or may not have tried. The feature aims to blend the strengths of both ANC and Transparency in a single mode.

And in iOS 27, Apple added a latest setting to let you conveniently fine-tune Adaptive Audio to your preferences.

Sources indicate that while wearing AirPods, open Control Center on your iPhone and tap the volume slider, then hit ‘Listening Mode’ in the bottom-left corner. Here you’ll see the standard listening mode options.

Fresh in iOS 27 though, when ‘Adaptive’ is selected, you can now use a Liquid Glass slider to adjust whether the mode lets in more or less external noise.

Slide it to the left and Adaptive Audio will more closely resemble Transparency, while sliding it to the right makes it cancel out more noise.

You can also move the latest slider incrementally to achieve exactly your ideal balance of Transparency and Noise Cancellation. It’s not limited to just a few preset options.

This Control Center slider is available on all AirPods models that support Adaptive Audio.

According to recent reports, do you ever use Adaptive Audio, and if so, have you adjusted it at all? Let us know in the comments.

Ray Dalio indicates Bessent move is sign that a debt crisis is getting closer; recommends gold and bitcoin

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's debt buyback announcement this week fits into a broader pattern that can signal a forthcoming crisis, according to billionaire investor Ray Dalio.
  • The Bridgewater Associates founder stated Bessent's blueprint to increase government debt purchases may portend trouble for the U.S.
  • Recent findings suggest that "I am confident that the government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote in a LinkedIn post published Friday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's debt buyback announcement this week fits into a broader pattern that can signal a forthcoming crisis, according to billionaire investor Ray Dalio.

The Bridgewater Associates founder stated Bessent's blueprint to increase government debt purchases may portend trouble for the U.S. economy. Coupled with the Japanese government reducing its U.S. bond market exposure and surging long-dated American bond yields, Dalio said investors may want to prepare their portfolios for increased risk by owning cryptocurrencies and gold.

Recent findings suggest that "I am confident that the government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote in a LinkedIn post published Friday. "If this is not dealt with now, the debts will build up to levels where they can't be managed without great trauma.".

Dalio noted that the Treasury Department has "only limited capacity" to buy back bonds. Bessent told CNBC on Thursday that his team was going to "make a market" and that the purchases would likely top $4 billion.

Sources indicate that the U.S. is spending about 40% more than it's bringing in, resulting in the burgeoning budget deficit, Dalio remarked. The U.S. budget deficit topped $432 billion in July, but Bessent told CNBC that it's likely peaked under President Donald Trump's administration.

According to recent reports, bessent remarked in the interview that a team was looking at ways to shrink spending by hundreds of billions of dollars. But Dalio said there is "very little ability" to do so given that it is either committed or considered essential.

After years of overspending, Dalio said total debt now dwarfs what the U.S. brings in each year. If the U.S. government was a business, Dalio said debt service payments would come in at roughly $11 trillion — about 200% of annual revenue.

Dalio, 77, warned the cost of repaying principal and servicing the debt will only grow over time.

To solve this, Dalio noted the U.S. needs to carefully employ a three-part strategy to get the budget deficit down to 3% of gross domestic product.

Recent findings suggest that first, Dalio noted the U.S. government needs to reduce its spending. Second, he said tax revenue needs to be raised. Finally, the Latest York native and Harvard Business School alumni said lower interest rates were needed.

Recent findings suggest that "All three need to happen concurrently so as to prevent any one from being too large," Dalio noted. "If any one is too large, the adjustment will be traumatic.".

Dalio cautioned against ramming through these adjustments by "force." For instance, "it would be very bad if the Federal Reserve unnaturally forced interest rates down," he stated.

According to recent reports, dalio remarked it's key to to take steps now, while the economy is healthy. An economy in recession requires increased government spending, he said.

Sources indicate that dalio mentioned the exact timing of a debt crisis can be swayed by variables ranging from military conflict to political change. On its current trajectory, the U.S. could enter such a crisis in as early as one year or as late as five. "My guess, which I suppose will be a bad one, is that it will come in three years, give or take two, if the course we're on is not changed.".

To prepare, Dalio recommended investors are underweight debt assets, such as bonds.

As much as 10% to 15% of a portfolio could land in gold, as well as "a bit" of bitcoin, the hedge fund founder noted.

Recent findings suggest that dalio's post came at the tail end of a volatile week for U.S. financial markets. Rising long-term Treasury yields have pressured stocks, leading the S&P 500 to snap a a three-week-long advance.
